resources.string:
ATA controls and automates your Tesla — no account, no Fleet API, no cloud.

▸ BASIC FEATURES
Open the Tesla app; jump to Charging/Climate/Controls/Location (may just open the app). Navigate Home/Work or any address (sent to the Tesla app, or Google Maps/Waze). Share a destination.

▸ BLE FEATURES
Enable under Settings → Behavior, status, Bluetooth & NFC, add your vehicle (VIN) and pair the phone key. Then lock/unlock, climate, charging, trunk/frunk, windows, sentry and more over Bluetooth, plus live status (battery, range, temperatures).

▸ MAKE IT YOURS
On the Vehicle or Favorites tab, long-press a tile to edit: drag to reorder, delete, re-add with +, star it for Favorites, then Save layout. Settings → Design sets multi-tiles and tiles per row. Pin any action as a shortcut, app-icon menu entry or widget (up to 8 tiles).

▸ AUTOMATION
Trigger actions from Samsung Routines or Tasker, and react to the car status (battery, charging, locked…) via ATA broadcasts.

Tip: set Home/Work addresses under Settings → Addresses — navigation works even without a saved vehicle.
Add a vehicle first to use the BLE actions.
The BLE features are in development and currently disabled. The basic features (navigation and opening the Tesla app) work now.

The phone acts as a Tesla NFC key card with its own key. Off by default; set it up with the assistant below. Works only while the phone is unlocked.

Pick an action. The shortcut contains your ATA token, so the app you create it in can run it as a trusted trigger.

Samsung Routines, the launcher and widgets start ATA shortcuts. They carry your personal ATA token, so ATA trusts them. Other apps, links and foreign NFC tags have no token and may only run Basic actions plus what you allow below.
Allow notifications so ATA can show results and ask for confirmations when a routine runs.
Run while the phone is locked
Non-critical BLE actions (climate, charging, lock …) also run when the phone is locked, e.g. in your pocket.
Unlock, trunk, frunk, charge port, vent windows and sentry off open the car. From automations they ask for a tap on a notification first. Tick an action to run it without asking (phone unlocked).
Risky: anyone holding your locked phone could trigger the ticked actions through a routine. Off by default.
BLE actions that apps without your ATA token (e.g. Tasker without the token extra) may run while the phone is unlocked. Critical actions are never allowed here.
After each status poll ATA sends org.tfv.ata.action.STATUS (battery, range, locked …). Every app on the phone can read it.
Add it as extra \"token\" in Tasker so its commands count as trusted. Renewing it invalidates copies in other apps; ATA updates its own shortcuts and widgets.
Tasker tasks using the old token stop working until you paste the new one. ATA shortcuts, widgets and routines using them are updated automatically.
Every NFC tag written so far stops working. Write new tags afterwards.
No confirmation from the car yet
Extra actions for routines (up to %1$d more on this device). The launcher menu keeps showing only the 4 actions above.
⚠️ Samsung Routines: which actions are available?

Routines can only start actions that ATA publishes as app shortcuts: the up to 4 actions of the icon menu, plus the extra routine actions chosen under Settings → Menu & widgets → Samsung Routines. Actions with a value (address, charge limit …) can\'t be used there. If an extra action doesn\'t show up in Routines on your device, only the 4 icon-menu actions work: put the ones you need into the icon menu.
Open apps on the phone (watch & automations)

Android only lets ATA open the Tesla app or navigation from the background (e.g. after a tap on the watch) if you allow \"Display over other apps\". Without it, ATA shows a notification you have to tap.
Allowed: taps on the watch and automations open the Tesla app / navigation directly on the phone.
Switch greyed out? Open App info → ATA → ⋮ → \"Allow restricted settings\", then try again.
Tap the notification on the phone to open it — or allow \"Display over other apps\" for ATA (Settings → Wear OS watch).
Opens the car: asks for confirmation when the tag is scanned
Bluetooth is off. Turn it on and try again.
Your phone becomes its own Tesla key (separate from the Tesla app\'s phone key, both work side by side). The car must allow it once: you confirm with a key card that already works with the car.
\"%1$s\" is not a valid VIN (17 characters, no I, O or Q).

The car screen asks you to confirm the new key. Place the plastic key card on the card reader in the center console (where you place it to drive). Do not hold this phone to the reader.
This phone can now control the car over Bluetooth. Tip: rename the key in the car under Controls → Locks.
If the car showed \"Key added\", everything is fine: just try a Bluetooth action. Otherwise start again and place the key card on the reader as soon as the car asks.

• Allow location for ATA and turn location on (Android hides the car's Bluetooth signal otherwise).
• Check the VIN (windscreen, bottom left, or vehicle registration).
• Stay in the car or within about 2 m.
• Wake the car: open a door or tap the screen.
• Turn Bluetooth off and on again.
Turn on Bluetooth (button above), then start again.
Allow \"Nearby devices\" (button above), then start again.

The car rejected the request (reason in brackets above). If the prompt on the car screen was cancelled, start again. If the problem stays, please send a bug report: it contains the exact reply of the car.
The car did not answer. Wake it (open a door) and start again.
Start again close to the car. If it keeps failing, restart Bluetooth on the phone.
Key ID of this phone (to find it in the car\'s key list)
Android asks \"Tesla or ATA\" at the card reader?

This appears when the phone is held to the car\'s card reader while both apps offer an NFC key. ATA\'s NFC key card is off by default since this version, so the Tesla app answers alone. For pairing you never need to hold the phone to the reader: use the plastic key card.
Tap a topic: what it does, the steps, and buttons that take you straight there. The status updates live.
Open Settings → Vehicles and tap +.\nEnter a name and the 17-character VIN (windscreen, bottom left, or vehicle registration).\nOptional: home and work address for navigation.

Choose up to 4 actions for the icon menu under "Menu & widgets": these appear as app shortcuts.
In Samsung Routines add an action → Apps → ATA and pick the shortcut.
Tasker & others: use "ATA shortcut" in the shortcut picker, every action is available there.
Under "Automation" choose what may run without opening the app.
Needed so that watch taps and routines can open the Tesla app or navigation while ATA is in the background.\nTap the button and allow \"Display over other apps\" for ATA.
Pick the actions for the widget under \"Menu & widgets\".\nLong-press the home screen → Widgets → ATA.\nPlace the action or status widget.

Get an NFC sticker (NTAG213/215/216).\nTap \"Write tag\", pick an action and hold the sticker to the back of the phone.\nFrom then on, tapping the phone on the sticker runs the action (e.g. in the car holder).

Install ATA on the watch (Play Store on the watch or the wear APK).
Pick the actions for the watch under "Wear OS watch": they sync automatically.
Taps on the watch run on the phone; "Open Tesla app" opens it on the phone.
Optional, so the watch works without the phone: "Wear OS watch" → "Pair watch" (assistant on the phone).

Turn on \"Direct BLE control\" and add a car with VIN.\nPair the phone once with the assistant (you need a working key card).\nThen the car tab, widgets and automations can lock, unlock, climate and more directly over Bluetooth.
Optional: the phone acts as an NFC key card.\nTurn on \"NFC key card\" in settings, then add it in the car like a card (Controls → Locks → Add key).\nThe phone only answers while it is unlocked.

The Tesla app is installed and already answers at the card reader. Keep ATA\'s NFC key card OFF: then there is no app chooser.\nIf you turn it on anyway, ATA only answers while ATA is open on screen. Otherwise the Tesla app answers as usual.\nDoes Android still ask? Open the NFC settings and check the default app for contactless use.
The phone answers at the car\'s card reader while it is unlocked.

The Tesla app is installed and uses the same card reader. So that Android doesn\'t ask \"Tesla or ATA\" every time, ATA\'s key card only answers while ATA is open. The rest of the time the Tesla app answers as usual.
Checks without pairing whether ATA finds the car over Bluetooth and gets an answer. Works while the Tesla app is connected too.
Connection works: the car answered (%1$s). You can pair now.
Log of the last attempt. If pairing doesn\'t work, copy it and send it along with your report.
Collects what is needed to find the problem: app and device info, setup and the Bluetooth logs of phone and watch. Run "Test connection" or the pairing first, then send the report.
Opens a prefilled GitHub issue. The full report is also in the clipboard: paste it if the log was shortened.
GitHub issues are public. The VIN is shortened; no keys or tokens are included.
Pair the watch\'s own key with the car, so it works without the phone. Guided from here.

The watch gets its own key (independent of the phone and the Tesla app). This assistant controls the watch from here: it shows what is missing, tests the connection and pairs. Keep ATA installed on the watch and the watch close to the car.
No watch connected to this phone.

Keep this screen open, the phone unlocked and NFC on.
In the car: Controls → Locks → Keys → "+ Add key".

The watch works like a Tesla key card: hold it to the B-pillar to unlock, place it on the card reader to drive. It uses its own key and only answers while it is unlocked on your wrist. This assistant controls the watch from here.
NFC on the watch turned on

Unlock: hold the watch face to the card reader on the driver\'s B-pillar. Drive: hold it on the card reader in the center console. The watch must be unlocked. If something doesn\'t work, send the bug report: it contains every request of the card reader to the watch.
Turn the watch key card off

Pair the watch with this phone in the Galaxy Wearable app (or Wear OS app) and keep Bluetooth on.\nInstall ATA on the watch (Play Store on the watch or the wear APK).\nOpen ATA on the watch once, then come back here.

Actions with a preset value, published as app shortcuts: Samsung Routines and the icon menu run them without asking. They share the space of the routine actions above.

No car position saved yet. ATA saves it automatically whenever it reaches the car over Bluetooth (status, commands), or tap \"Parked here\" next to the car.
The car position is the phone\'s GPS position the last time ATA reached the car over Bluetooth, so it is accurate to a few metres. Hold the phone flat for the compass.
Some functions depend on the vehicle (e.g. opening doors, power liftgate) and don\'t work on every model.

Big tiles on the watch\'s first screen. Round watches arrange them in rows of 1/2/1 or 2/3/2, square watches as 2×2 or 3×3. Swipe left on the watch for all other actions and the settings.

On the watch, long-press the watch face → Edit → Complications → ATA. Status values are offered separately: battery, range, inside and outside temperature, lock state. The four action slots run the action chosen here.
The first %1$d chosen actions appear as tiles, the others in the list (swipe left).
Battery, range, inside and outside temperature, charging and lock state, in every size.
Neon: glowing lines (standard). Material: calm Material 3 surfaces and a painted car that looks like the real one. Both in light and dark.
The compass is unsure: move the phone in a figure 8 a few times.

Position still rough (±%1$d m): the direction may be off. Wait a moment or step outside.
Unlocks the car once when you walk up to it with the phone, measured by the strength of the car\'s Bluetooth signal. Only after you were away from the car, never twice in a row.
Also while the phone is locked
Off: with the phone locked, ATA asks with a notification first.

The distance is approximate (signal strength depends on the car, phone, pocket and surroundings): try it out and adjust. A quiet notification shows while proximity unlock is on. Needs Bluetooth and location access.
Turn on Direct BLE control first.
Look, theme, car view and tiles
Bundle related actions in one tile (lock/unlock, seats, volume …). Off: one tile per action.
Auto: 3 on phones, more on tablets. Names stay visible at every size.
No favorites yet. Long-press a tile in the vehicle tab and tap ☆.
Look of the home-screen widgets (status, actions, find car). They follow the app\'s light / dark theme.
The wallpaper shines through a little.
Shows a made-up, connected car (50 %, charging) so you can try everything without a Tesla. Nothing is sent. Starts from the same state each time it is turned on.
Only when you ask: pull down on the vehicle tab or tap ↻. No reads in the background.
When the app starts, then regularly while the car is plugged in and the phone is in use.
At a fixed interval, also in the background (5 min to 3 h).
Requires the BLE features. Automatic reads never wake the car: while it sleeps only the lock state is refreshed. Pulling down wakes it.
Switching from the GitHub version to the Play Store version

Export and import your layout and appearance settings and your VIN, made for switching from the GitHub version to the Play Store version. How it works: export in the GitHub version (1.9.7 or later), import in the Play Store version. Afterwards we recommend uninstalling the old app. Both apps can also stay installed side by side. The file is unencrypted and contains your VIN, so keep it safe and don\'t share it publicly. Vehicle keys are not included and need to be paired again once.
